learning_objective: 🎯 Master organic substitution! Learn how halogens attach to carbon chains and rings, changing their properties and making them the ultimate building blocks of organic synthesis.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) are much more electronegative than Carbon. They pull the shared electrons towards themselves, making the Carbon slightly positive (hungry for electrons) and the Halogen slightly negative.

SN2 is a fast, 1-step 'back-attack' where the incoming molecule kicks the halogen out directly, flipping the molecule's shape like an umbrella in the wind. SN1 is a 2-step process where the halogen leaves first, forming a positive Carbon (carbocation), before the new molecule attaches.

If a carbon is attached to four completely different groups, it is 'Chiral'. Just like your left and right hands, chiral molecules have mirror images that cannot be perfectly superimposed on each other (enantiomers).

Instead of substitution, haloalkanes can undergo 'beta-elimination' when heated with alcoholic KOH. The halogen and a neighboring hydrogen are removed, leaving behind a double bond (an alkene) following Zaitsev's rule.

When a halogen is attached directly to a benzene ring, it's very hard to remove. The lone pair of electrons on the halogen partakes in resonance with the ring, giving the C-X bond a partial double-bond character.

fun_activity.title: 🖐️ The Chirality Hands Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Place your left hand exactly over your right hand (both palms facing up). They look identical, but they don't perfectly superimpose (your thumbs point opposite ways). Molecules act the exact same way—these are called 'chiral' molecules or enantiomers!

exam_tips: 📌 SN2 reactions are fastest in primary ($1^\circ$) alkyl halides because of less steric hindrance (crowding). SN1 reactions are fastest in tertiary ($3^\circ$) halides because they form the most stable carbocations.
📌 Always mention Markovnikov's or Anti-Markovnikov's rule when describing the addition of HX to asymmetrical alkenes.
📌 Haloarenes undergo Electrophilic Substitution (like nitration or halogenation) specifically at the Ortho and Para positions because the halogen is 'ortho-para directing'.
quick_recap: ⭐ An SN2 reaction results in complete 'inversion' of configuration, while SN1 results in 'racemization' (a 50/50 mix).
⭐ Haloalkanes are generally heavier and have higher boiling points than their parent hydrocarbons.
⭐ Grignard reagents ($R-Mg-X$) must be prepared in strictly dry, anhydrous conditions because they react instantly and violently with water.
